title: Optional: build a package from source: log, Cancel and missing tools
covers: PackageSourceDialog build path, Cancel, missing tool, Install it for me
context: From the wizard of Get this package, Let Archipelia build it downloads the source of the project, shows what it will do, builds in a private folder with a live log and installs the result. A missing compiler or other tool is explained, with a link, Show me how, Install it for me and Check again. OPTIONAL: building runs the code of a third party project on this PC.
changed: packages/design PackageSourceDialog build steps and tool steps
packages/engine source build, sandbox and the missing tool check

setup.label: WARNING
setup.text: Building runs third party code on your PC with your user rights and Archipelia cannot check it. Skip this test unless you trust the project you pick.

setup.label: scope
setup.text: The build step says either that the build runs in a sandbox, or that it runs with your user rights. Read which one before you go on.

setup.label: tools
setup.text: A missing tool can be installed by Archipelia only after you press Install on the step that shows the command, the size and the licence. Do that only if you accept the licence.

setup.label: world
setup.text: Chrono Trigger Rando-Dalton Imperial (previous test), network needed. A build can take several minutes.

steps: Open Games, tab Archipelago index, search the world and press Get this package. Press Next, then Use this one on a project you trust that contains ctrando, tick the trust box and press Next.

On What we found pick Build it from its source code, Next, then Let Archipelia build it, Next. The step Download the source warns that building runs the code of the project with your access and that nothing is downloaded yet.

Read the sandbox or user rights line. Press Back, then Next: you return to the same step. Press Download the source. The step Getting the source says it is downloading and setting up a private build folder.
Check the build tools shows the source with a short commit, Archive size, a sha256 line and Build tools Archipelia will install in the private folder (or none needed). Press Check and build.
The step Build says Building ctrando. This can take a few minutes, and the Build log fills with lines. Press Cancel while it builds: the build stops, the log stops growing and nothing is installed.
Start again and let the build run to the end. Result A, success: Packages to install, Install and Done follow, Done says the game is installed and ready, and the card moves to Installed.
Result B, a tool is missing: a step named Install and the tool shows a title such as The Microsoft C++ Build Tools are missing, a link, and the choices Show me how and Install it for me.
Install it for me shows the command, size, source and licence. Archipelia installs only after you press Install. Check again re-runs the build.
Result C, the build failed: The build failed shows the log, Copy log and Try again.
For result A press Remove on the card and Delete, so the world is not left behind.
pass: Nothing is downloaded until you press Download the source, and the warning comes before it.
The tools step shows the source, commit, size, checksum and build tools. The log shows live output while it builds.
Cancel stops the build with nothing installed.
The build ends in a success, a missing tool step with a link, Show me how, Install it for me and Check again, or a build failed page with the log.
fail: Anything is downloaded or built before the click on Download the source.
Cancel leaves the build running (the log keeps growing) or leaves a half installed world.
A missing tool shows a code, a stack or a blank line instead of a sentence, or Archipelia installs a tool without you pressing Install.
The wizard freezes with no log and no Cancel.
notes: OPTIONAL. Skip it if you do not trust any project in the list. Stopping at the Download the source step is a fine partial result: say so in your note.
On Windows a C++ compiler is often missing. Seeing the missing tool step with its choices is a valid pass for the detection.
Say in your note which project you built and which result you got (A, B or C).
